case_name: Nagar Nigam, Meerut v Al Faheem Meat Exports Private Limited and Others
respondent: Al Faheem Meat Exports Private Limited
facts: Nagar Nigam, Meerut is before us questioning the legality of a judgment and order dated 29th March, 2006 passed by a Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court in Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 53782 of 2004.
The first respondent herein was granted a licence for a period of one year to run a slaughter house which is owned by the appellant-Corporation.
It gives this slaughter house on annual licence basis.
Such a licence was granted to the first respondent herein on 9 January 2004.
The said licence expired on 8 January 2005.
The impugned advertisement dated 6 December 2004 was issued by the appellant inviting applications for granting a fresh contract for running the slaughter house.
It is this advertisement whose validity was challenged before the High Court.
In the year 2003, the Mayor of the Nagar Nigam issued an advertisement on 9 November 2003 for modernizing the existing slaughter house, which was published in some local newspapers.
The first respondent is said to have submitted a project report in response to the same.

However, as stated in paragraph 8 of the counter affidavit of the Nagar Nigam before the High Court, the power to accept such a project report is with the general body of the Nagar Nigam, which has not granted any approval thereto.
It is alleged by the first respondent that he sent a representation to the State Government seeking its permission to modernize the slaughter house.
Thereafter he filed a writ petition being Writ No. 37187/2004 before the High Court, which disposed off the same on 15.9.2004 by directing the State Government to consider the said representation.
It is alleged that instead of deciding the representation, the Nagar Nigam issued the impugned advertisement inviting applications for tenders for running of the slaughter house in question.
The State intended to acquire some land for a site for construction of an alternative slaughter house, in respect of which proceeding under the Land Acquisition Act was initiated.

However, at the instance of one of the owners of the said land, the High Court in Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 11069 of 2006 (Asaf Ali vs. State of U.P. & Ors.) stayed dispossession of the petitioner therein.
That writ petition is said to be still pending.

The High Court by means of the impugned judgment dated 29 March 2006 has allowed the writ petition directing that the writ petitioner (respondent No. 1 herein) should be allowed to run the slaughter house for 10 years on terms and conditions stipulated therein.
issues: What is the validity of the impugned advertisement dated 6 December 2004 issued by the appellant inviting applications for granting a fresh contract for running the slaughter house?
Is the Nagar Nigam entitled to grant a licence for running the slaughter house without following the procedure laid down in Chapter XVI of the Act?
Can the first respondent be allowed to run the slaughter house for 10 years on terms and conditions stipulated by the High Court?
petitioner_arguments: The impugned advertisement dated 6 December 2004 is invalid as it was issued without following the procedure laid down in Chapter XVI of the Act.
The Nagar Nigam has no power to grant a licence for running the slaughter house without following the procedure laid down in Chapter XVI of the Act.
The first respondent should be allowed to run the slaughter house for 10 years on terms and conditions stipulated by the High Court.
respondent_arguments: The impugned advertisement dated 6 December 2004 is valid as it was issued after considering the representations made by the first respondent.
The Nagar Nigam has the power to grant a licence for running the slaughter house without following the procedure laid down in Chapter XVI of the Act.
The first respondent should not be allowed to run the slaughter house for 10 years on terms and conditions stipulated by the High Court.
court_reasoning: The interest of the common man at large is paramount which should not be ignored and to ensure the welfare of the local residents by saving them from facing untold hardships and sufferings.

We direct the Nigam and other concerned authorities of Meerut, Administration to assist and cooperate with petitioner No. 1 to modernize the Slaughter House at its existing site on following 'terms and conditions' :-

Petitioner No. 1 represented by its Director Mohd. Imran Khan (which includes legal representative, successor, assignee, agent, nominee, servant etc.) shall, on or before 30 April 2006, file an affidavit giving undertaking to the Nigam to comply with the directions given hereunder.
Petitioner No. 1 as per its offer and undertaking given to the court shall on or before 15th May 2006 deposit Rs. three crores with Nagar Nigam, Meerut.
Petitioner No. 1 shall also deposit Rs. two crores on or before 30th September 2006 with Nagar Nigam, Meerut.
holding: The High Court by means of the impugned judgment dated 29 March 2006 has allowed the writ petition directing that the writ petitioner (respondent No. 1 herein) should be allowed to run the slaughter house for 10 years on terms and conditions stipulated therein.

The Nigam and other concerned authorities of Meerut, Administration are directed to assist and cooperate with petitioner No. 1 to modernize the Slaughter House at its existing site on following 'terms and conditions' :-
Petitioner No. 1 shall file an affidavit giving undertaking to the Nigam to comply with the directions given hereunder.
Petitioner No. 1 shall deposit Rs. three crores with Nagar Nigam, Meerut on or before 15th May 2006.
Petitioner No. 1 shall also deposit Rs. two crores on or before 30th September 2006 with Nagar Nigam, Meerut.
